item.title: DreamStream: Towards Policy-Oriented Generative Simulation for End-to-End Driving
item.description: Faithfully evaluating end-to-end driving policies in simulation requires observations that are not merely photo-realistic, but preserve the scene features a policy relies on to make decisions. Existing platforms, however, exhibit a sim-to-real visual gap that corrupts policy perception, undermining their ability to assess a policy's closed-loop decision-making. item.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
item.description: A multi-agent system can reduce latency on complex tasks by executing work concurrently. Several pioneering harness frameworks support multi-agent systems. However, the scalability of current multi-agent harnesses is often constrained by a central orchestrator's capacity to allocate tasks and coordinate workers. item.description: Collaboration topology shapes both the performance and execution cost of LLM-based multi-agent systems. item.description: Humanoid robots require diverse embodied experiences to acquire complex loco-manipulation and collaborative skills. item.description: Social norms cannot be identified from behavior alone: the same cooperative equilibrium may reflect shared expectations, strategic incentives, or simple imitation. item.description: Camera-based 3D object detection and online vectorized HD mapping provide compact scene representations for autonomous driving, but both depend on accurate metric geometry and remain limited by depth ambiguity. item.title: Calibration Is Not Verification: Falsifiability-Aware Conformal Routing for Mixture-of-Agents

item.title: Destination Support Restoration for Finite-Set Multimodal Trajectory Prediction
item.description: Robots operating around pedestrians often reason over a finite set of predicted human futures. item.description: Analog circuit sizing remains a challenging and time-consuming task due to the large design space, strong performance trade-offs, and increasing circuit complexity in scaled technologies. item.title: Sometimes You Gotta Run Before You Can Walk: Run-then-Walk Scheduling Strategy for VLM Autonomous Driving
item.description: Recent VLM-based autonomous driving planners adopt GRPO-style reinforcement learning to optimize driving performance. item.title: Protocol before progress: leakage-aware evaluation of AIS trajectory prediction
item.description: Reported gains in vessel-trajectory prediction from Automatic Identification System (AIS) data are credited to new architectures, but the evaluation protocol is rarely measured as a source of error reduction. item.title: CogenPVG: Cognitive-Enhanced Reflective Multi-Agent Framework for Persuasive Video Generation
item.description: Persuasive video generation (PVG) is a valuable yet under-explored research topic. Despite the significant advances in multimodal content generation, AI-empowered automated creation of human-made-like videos with substantial persuasiveness remains a formidable challenge. item.description: Graphical User Interface (GUI) Agents autonomously interact with software to fulfill user requests, where GUI navigation stands out as the most critical and challenging capability. item.title: MedVLA: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Framework for Closed-Loop Precision Medical Robot Manipulation
item.description: Precision medical robotics demands adaptive decision-making under strict safety, interpretability, and execution constraints. Although recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models show strong multimodal reasoning ability, their continuous action generation paradigm is not well suited for precision medical tasks, where reliable closed-loop operation may also depend on non-action system function calls. item.description: We study distributed Byzantine-resilient actor-critic multi-agent reinforcement learning (AC-MARL), where agents collectively learn policies through local interactions. item.title: SambaGraph: Action-Reaction Spatio-Temporal Graphs for Soccer Tactical Response Modeling
